weaknesses.mistake: LC 643: the basic solution was independent, but the optimal O(n) approach needed a hint.
weaknesses.correct: Update the fixed-size window incrementally instead of recomputing its sum.
weaknesses.exercise: Re-solve LC 643 without a hint and explain the incremental O(n) update.

weaknesses.topic: Sliding window: variable-size recognition and application
weaknesses.mistake: LC 209 could not be solved; LC 567 needed a hint. LC 438 and LC 1004 were solved independently.
weaknesses.correct: State the window invariant and the exact shrinking condition before coding.
weaknesses.cause: Not established. Variable and frequency windows are developing but inconsistent.
weaknesses.exercise: Unseen variable-size and frequency-window problems without hints, starting with LC 209.

weaknesses.topic: Sliding window: generalization and invariant derivation
weaknesses.mistake: LC 643 optimal, LC 209, LC 567 and LC 424 all needed help or failed, while LC 3, 438 and 1004 were independent.
weaknesses.correct: Recognize the pattern, then derive the invariant, window movement and complexity for the specific problem.
weaknesses.cause: Not established. The evidence does not support blaming memorization, rushing or any single cause.
weaknesses.exercise: An unseen mixed sliding-window problem with the pattern unnamed. Require recognition, invariant, movement, complexity, independent C++ and edge cases.

weaknesses.mistake: Described browser event handlers only; left out DNS, TCP, TLS, the HTTP request and response, and the server path.
weaknesses.correct: Loading a URL is an HTTP request preceded by DNS, TCP and TLS. Button clicks trigger further HTTP requests handled by routes.
weaknesses.exercise: Lesson 1 questions A to C, then trace one authenticated route in the internship API.

weaknesses.mistake: Answered a last-seat booking scenario as a deadlock and left the shared-counter question blank, although races were studied on 2026-08-18.
weaknesses.correct: Concurrent read-modify-write without atomicity causes a lost update or double booking. Fix it with atomic operations, locks or transactions.
weaknesses.cause: Retention and transfer gap. Nothing further is established.
weaknesses.exercise: Closed-book scenarios in Weeks 2 and 3: booking, counter, compare-and-set.

weaknesses.mistake: The crash answer covered durable state but not acknowledgement, redelivery, duplicates or idempotency.
weaknesses.correct: At-least-once delivery produces duplicates, so handlers must be idempotent.
weaknesses.exercise: Week 5: walk a worker crash after processing but before acknowledgement, and design the retry and idempotency path.

weaknesses.topic: Internship ownership: cannot trace the job worker
weaknesses.mistake: Could not describe what the background job worker does or how it handles failure.
weaknesses.correct: Be able to trace trigger, claim, process, finish or fail, and retry from the source, unaided.
weaknesses.cause: Not yet studied from source by you.
weaknesses.exercise: Source traces in Weeks 1 and 5; mark uncertain lines as unsure.

dailyDsa: One unseen problem, 30 to 35 minutes, C++, no hints. Say the pattern, invariant and complexity aloud.
If stuck at the timer, use the hint ladder: pattern name, then invariant, then approach. Any hint means not independent, and it is logged.
One spaced retest of an earlier failed or hinted problem, 3 to 7 days later.
Log problem, pattern, independence, hints, time and space complexity, mistakes and edge cases.

portfolio.title: Publishable portfolio project (Weeks 5 to 8, Saturdays)
portfolio.body: A small reliable job queue: at-least-once delivery, idempotency keys, retry with backoff and jitter, graceful shutdown and fault-injection tests, with a design doc and benchmarks you measure yourself. It is not proprietary, so it can be public, and it doubles as the system design story.
